sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Radioligand binding confirmed ligand-binding competence; flow cytometry confirmed surface display of the tagged receptor in AtT20 cells — both function and surface expression preserved.
sites.rationale: AVPR1B has no signal peptide (topology landmarks: extracellular 1–33, TM1 34–58), so the N-terminus is extracellular and a prepended tag (insert_after_residue=0) is not cleaved. The paper's flow cytometry assay requires the Myc epitope to be surface-accessible, and the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of this GPCR; ECL1/2/3 are loops, not termini. The insert point sits 33 residues from TM1, well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. Radioligand binding confirms the tagged receptor retains function. AVPR1B (V1b/V3 receptor) expressed in AtT20 corticotroph cells as a dual GFP+Myc-tagged full-length construct. Flow cytometry with anti-Myc antibody was used to quantify surface export; radioligand binding confirmed receptor function. The Myc epitope must be extracellular for flow cytometry detection without permeabilization. AVPR1B is a GPCR with no signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–33) is the sole extracellular terminus, making it the only position consistent with surface-accessible Myc detection.

sources.claim: Little is known about endoplasmic reticulum (ER) export signals, particularly those of members of the G-protein-coupled receptor family. We investigated the structural motifs involved in membrane export of the human pituitary vasopressin V1b/V3 receptor. A series of V3 receptors carrying deletions and point mutations were expressed in AtT20 corticotroph cells. We analyzed the export of these receptors by monitoring radioligand binding and by analysis of a V3 receptor tagged with both green fluorescent protein and Myc epitopes by a novel flow cytometry-based method.

literature_notes: L1 is the sole ledger line. It reports a full-length, membrane-anchored AVPR1B construct carrying both a Myc epitope and GFP, validated by flow cytometry (surface) and radioligand binding (function) in AtT20 cells. The quote names no residue and no specific loop; position is topology_derived to the N-terminal prepend because (a) the Myc tag must be extracellular for the flow cytometry assay, (b) AVPR1B has no signal peptide so the N-terminus is extracellular and not cleaved, and (c) the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus of this 7-TM receptor. Confidence is medium rather than high because the exact junction residue is not stated in the quote. The GFP tag is placed in other_positions as intracellular (C-terminal fusion, standard for GPCRs). No ledger evidence supports any ECL insertion for AVPR1B.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP fused to the same AVPR1B construct; C-terminus (residues 342–424) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so the GFP tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-tag site.
